summary: WebSocket ping/pong-induced half-close causes missing final chunk and stalled EOF
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed that long-running WebSocket streaming sessions intermittently complete without the final text fragment and never emit the terminal EOF/metadata. Sessions show normal tokens for the majority of the response, then a short silent period followed by a websocket close (1006/abrupt) from the edge. No server-side application error is logged at the time of the close.

Impact:
- Several CartaTech users report truncated summaries in production workflows; visible data-loss for final sentences/metadata.
- Affects dedicated customers behind managed edge proxies and long-running generations (>12s).

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: prod-us-west
- Client: browser-based WS client + mobile app (both observed)
- Model: redwood-suite-7b-instruct, typical sequence length 512-1024 tokens

Observed behavior:
- Server logs show normal stream of chunks, last logged server chunk is immediately followed by an edge-level FIN without the standard terminal metadata event.
- Edge shows a ping/pong exchange with an out-of-order PONG arriving while kernel socket is in write half-close.
- Client receives final token subset, then websocket abrupt close (1006). When client reconnects and attempts resume, resume offset is mismatched by a few bytes and resume fails to re-emit missing sentence.

Expected behavior:
- Websocket keepalive (ping/pong) should not induce midstream half-close or drop terminal event. Resume should align offsets and re-stream trailing tokens or provide terminal metadata.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long streaming generation (>12s) via websocket on redwood-suite-7b-instruct
2) Put an edge-proxy between client and Redwood API with aggressive ping interval (10s) and small socket send buffer configured
3) Start generation, wait for >10s of streaming tokens, observe client receives most tokens then silent gap then unexpected close
4) Reconnect client and attempt resume; observe offset mismatch and missing terminal event
logs: [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T15:21:03.131Z DEBUG half-close detected on fd=42, no error from app
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: aggressive ping/pong at the edge causes a race where the proxy sends a ping while server is in the middle of writing a final frame; proxy then interprets partial write as half-close and issues RST rather than allowing graceful drain.

What we looked at so far:
- RT logs show no application exception.
- Kernel-level traces (tcpdump) show FIN coming from proxy ~1-3ms after last server write.
- Resume code path assumes idempotent message boundaries and exact byte offsets; small window where proxy coalesces control frames can shift offsets by a few bytes and break resume.

Temporary mitigations tested:
- Increasing proxy ping interval to 45s prevented reproducer in a controlled env.
- Disabling Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) on the serving runtime reduced coalescing but we need to evaluate perf impact.

Next steps:
- Request edge/proxy team to run a controlled test with ping/pong disabled for a session and capture tcpdump.
- Add defensive trimming in resume logic to tolerate +/- N bytes and replay trailing tokens if terminal metadata missing.
- Create PR to server runtime to ensure terminal metadata is flushed with an explicit flush event and sequence-anchor before allowing control-frame processing.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports truncated summaries in multiple user sessions, visible in prod. Assigned to Eng for triage.
Eng (Jonah): Captured tcpdump and confirmed proxy FIN arrives immediately after last server write; opening kernel-level tracing ticket.
SRE (Marta Lopez): Temporarily increased keepalive interval for CartaTech in prod-us-west to 60s to reduce occurrence; monitoring.
Customer (CartaTech support): Thanks, we see fewer truncations after keepalive change but one case still occurred at 03/11 09:14 UTC; sent requested logs.
resolution: Workaround: SRE increased edge keepalive/ping interval to 60s for CartaTech and reduced aggressive connection reuse. Scoped server change: emit explicit terminal-flush anchor before allowing control frames to be processed. Planned fix: PR to serving-runtime to add terminal-anchor flush and resume-tolerance (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/917). Follow-up: edge-runbook update to avoid aggressive ping intervals for long-lived WS streams.
related_action_items: Edge runbook update: avoid sub-20s ping for WS long streams
Resume-tolerance test cases to be added to e2e streaming tests
